lines.text: Could lightning power the world? Catch every bolt, for a whole year.
lines.phonemes: kʊd lˈaɪtnɪŋ pˈaʊɚ ðə wˈɜːld? kˈætʃ ˈɛvɹi bˈoʊlt, fɚɹə hˈoʊl jˈɪɹ.

lines.text: Lightning is flashing somewhere right now, about forty-four times every second, all around the planet. That adds up to more than a billion flashes in a year.
lines.phonemes: lˈaɪtnɪŋ ɪz flˈæʃɪŋ sˈʌmwɛɹ ɹˈaɪt nˈaʊ, ɐbˌaʊt fˈɔːɹɾifˈɔːɹ tˈaɪmz ˈɛvɹi sˈɛkənd, ˈɔːl ɚɹˈaʊnd ðə plˈænɪt. ðæt ˈædz ˌʌp tə mˈɔːɹ ðˌænə bˈɪliən flˈæʃᵻz ɪn ɐ jˈɪɹ.

lines.text: One flash carries roughly a billion joules, a rough guess with a wide range. Multiply it by every flash in the year.
lines.phonemes: wˈʌn flˈæʃ kˈæɹiz ɹˈʌfli ɐ bˈɪliən dʒˈuːlz, ɐ ɹˈʌf ɡˈɛs wɪð ɐ wˈaɪd ɹˈeɪndʒ. mˌʌltɪplˈaɪ ɪt baɪ ˈɛvɹi flˈæʃ ɪnðə jˈɪɹ.

lines.text: That is about four hundred billion kilowatt-hours. But a number only means something beside another, so let's compare it with what we use.
lines.phonemes: ðæt ɪz ɐbˌaʊt fˈɔːɹ hˈʌndɹɪd bˈɪliən kˈɪləwˌɑːtˈaʊɚz. bˌʌt ɐ nˈʌmbɚɹ ˈoʊnli mˈiːnz sˈʌmθɪŋ bᵻsˌaɪd ɐnˈʌðɚ, sˌoʊ lˈɛts kəmpˈɛɹ ɪt wɪð wʌt wiː jˈuːz.

lines.text: The world uses nearly eighty times more electricity in a year. All the lightning on Earth would run it for about five days.
lines.phonemes: ðə wˈɜːld jˈuːsᵻz nˌɪɹli ˈeɪɾi tˈaɪmz mˈɔːɹ ᵻlɛktɹˈɪsᵻɾi ɪn ɐ jˈɪɹ. ˈɔːl ðə lˈaɪtnɪŋ ˌɔn ˈɜːθ wʊd ɹˈʌn ɪt fɔːɹ ɐbˌaʊt fˈaɪv dˈeɪz.

lines.text: If a flash holds ten times less or ten times more, it swings from half a day to about seven weeks.
lines.phonemes: ɪf ɐ flˈæʃ hˈoʊldz tˈɛn tˈaɪmz lˈɛs ɔːɹ tˈɛn tˈaɪmz mˈɔːɹ, ɪt swˈɪŋz fɹʌm hˈæf ɐ dˈeɪ tʊ ɐbˌaʊt sˈɛvən wˈiːks.

lines.text: Catching it is the real problem. Most of a flash becomes heat, light and sound, and each bolt is over in a split second.
lines.phonemes: kˈætʃɪŋ ɪɾ ɪz ðə ɹˈiːəl pɹˈɑːbləm. mˈoʊst əv ɐ flˈæʃ bɪkˌʌmz hˈiːt, lˈaɪt ænd sˈaʊnd, ænd ˈiːtʃ bˈoʊlt ɪz ˌoʊvɚɹ ɪn ɐ splˈɪt sˈɛkənd.
